mechanisms: Cost is a binding constraint: adoption favors a service when it is cheaper than the traditional method it replaces.
Convenience is a binding constraint: adoption favors a service when it provides anytime-anywhere access that saves time and fits existing digital habits.
Trust is a binding constraint: adoption favors a service when security measures are visible and the institution is known and trusted; when trust is absent, human interaction is preferred.
Self-efficacy is a binding constraint: adoption favors a service when the user already possesses the skills and the device-and-data infrastructure to use it.
Social proof is a contributing factor: adoption is more likely when peers already use a service and the user identifies with a youth-oriented, socially-driven innovation.
objection_patterns: Is this cheaper than what I already use?
Can I access it anytime, anywhere, without extra effort?
Do I trust this institution, and can I see the security measures?
Do I have the skills and the data to use this without help?
